topic: sub:12|Relative frequency and probability|Use relative frequency as an estimate of probability

parts.latex: What is the relative frequency of a student eating fast food at least 3 times in one week?

solutions.latex:
At least 3 times means $3$, $4$ or $5$ times, with frequencies $20$, $18$ and $15$.

$$\begin{aligned} \text{Relative frequency} &= \dfrac{20+18+15}{78} \\ &= \dfrac{53}{78} \end{aligned}$$

meta.format_note: Criteria row added. Table frequency labels (3, 4, 5 times) assumed from the source numbers; not visible in text.

parts.latex:
The relative frequency of basketball is $\dfrac{2}{5}$

Use the data in the table to determine the number of students who play basketball on weekends.

A sample of 50 students is to be undertaken to analyse their level of enjoyment in playing their weekend sport.

How many students who play cricket on the weekend, should be included in the sample?

solutions.latex:
The relative frequency of basketball is $\dfrac{2}{5}$, so the other sports make up $\dfrac{3}{5}$ of the total, and they total $150$ students.
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Total students} &= \dfrac{150}{3}\times 5 \\ &= 250 \end{aligned}$$
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Basketball} &= 250-150 \\ &= 100 \end{aligned}$$
Therefore 100 students play basketball.
criteria: Finds the total number of students, or equivalent merit

meta.format_note: Rubric written by us. The 150 for other sports is taken from the source working; the table is not shown here.

solutions.latex:
The sample is proportional: 60 of the 250 students play cricket.
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Cricket in sample} &= \dfrac{60}{250}\times 50 \\ &= 12 \end{aligned}$$

meta.format_note: Rubric written by us. The 60 cricket players is from the table, not shown here.

figures.cap: frequency table of spinner colours, Orange blank

parts.latex:
A spinner with different coloured sectors is spun 40 times. The results are recorded in the table. What is the relative frequency of obtaining the colour orange?

\exfigure{827_q1_1}

solutions.latex:
The spinner is spun 40 times, so the frequencies sum to 40.

The frequency of orange is $x$, where $40=x+34$, so $x=6$.

$$\begin{aligned} \text{Relative frequency} &= \dfrac{6}{40} \\ &= \dfrac{3}{20} \end{aligned}$$

Hence the correct option is the one equal to $\dfrac{3}{20}$.

meta.format_note: Working relies on the table in the figure (other frequencies sum to 34).

827_q1_1.notes: Frequency table, transcribed rather than drawn (rule 8). Headers are italic on the paper; the Orange frequency is an empty answer box, kept as a boxed blank.

figures.cap: cumulative frequency histogram of lollies per packet

parts.latex:
A company manufacturing packets of lollies advertises them as '25 lollies per packet'.

A sample of packets was collected and the number of lollies in each packet were counted. The results are displayed in the cumulative frequency histogram below.

\exfigure{828_q21_1}

If a packet is chosen at random, what is the probability that it contains at least 25 lollies?

solutions.latex:
The probability of at least $25$ lollies is the complement of fewer than $25$ lollies.
$$\begin{aligned} P(\geq 25) &= 1 - P(< 25) \\ &= 1 - \dfrac{10}{35} \\ &= \dfrac{25}{35} \\ &\approx 71.4\% \end{aligned}$$
criteria: Indicates the total number of packets is $35$, or finds that $25$ packets have at least $25$ lollies, or equivalent merit

meta.source_flag: Source writes $P(<24)$ in the complement of 'at least 25'; I changed it to $P(<25)$, which is the correct complement, value 10/35 unchanged.
